questions.prompt: When a model makes a tool call for a function you defined, who runs the function?

options.text: The model runs it inside its own response.
options.explanation: The Claude docs say the model never executes anything on its own. It only emits a structured request.

options.text: Your application runs it and sends the result back.
options.explanation: Right. Your code runs the call, which also lets it check the call first.

options.text: Nobody. The model only describes the call in text and pretends it happened.
options.explanation: The call is real. Your code must run it and return a result, or the model has nothing to work with.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a sign, per the Claude docs, that you should use a tool?

options.text: You need the model to translate a paragraph.
options.explanation: The Claude docs list translation as a task the model can do from training alone.

options.text: You want a short, friendly greeting message.
options.explanation: Nothing needs to run, so there is nothing for a tool to do.

options.text: You parse the model's text with a regex to find a decision.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say that decision should have been a tool call.

options.text: The user writes in a language other than English and wants a reply in English.
options.explanation: Language does not decide it. Tools are for actions, outside data and guaranteed structure.

questions.prompt: Are tool definitions free to send with every request?

options.text: No. OpenAI and Anthropic both count them as input tokens.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say definitions count against the context limit and are billed as input tokens. Claude also adds a tool-use system prompt.

options.text: Yes. Only the tool calls the model actually makes are billed.
options.explanation: The names, descriptions and schemas are sent on every request, so they are billed every time.
